skin-accent.note: Forwarded live from the running Hermes One skin (gold in default/dark, purple in catppuccin/light). Marks selection only, never condition — including the 3px left edge on a row an instruction sent the operator to. The hex is the fail-safe for an unreadable shell.

accent-fg.note: Near-black, not #fff: the host declares this only under :root.dark, so in every light skin the fallback lands on the one filled button, where #fff measured 1.1:1 against the paper-white fail-safe accent.

ok.note: Fill/dot form. As text it measured 1.49:1 worst case, so words use ok-text.

warn.note: The router needs attention: an exception count, a rule that never fired, an expensive window, a missing billing mode, an id the catalogue does not know. Never the operator's own doing.

bad.note: Reserved for a control giving way — including the state word 'banido' on a manual ban's row. Rejection reasons under a DROPPED heading stay muted.

info.note: Worst raw-text case measured across 23 palettes x both polarities: 1.38:1 in neon-paint/light. Hence the -text forms.

ok-text.note: 45% is the measured ratio for all four: worst case 5.08:1 (info, neon-paint/light) against a 4.5:1 floor; 50% gives 4.44:1 and does not clear it. Mixing toward TEXT rather than away from BG is what makes it darken on parchment and lighten on navy. The @supports guard is required because a custom property accepts any token stream at parse time, so an engine without color-mix would keep the declaration and fail at computed-value time.

plane-raised.note: The host's authored wash, not a mix toward --text: measured, mixing toward the text colour INVERTS in catppuccin/light (bg #EFF1F5, surface #FFFFFF), so a raised plane read as recessed.

hairline.note: The system's only structural device: group boundaries, row separators, sequence spines, the inset edge on a dot.

muted.note: The second and last text step. It bottoms out at 3.47:1 across 21 skins x both polarities; a third step derived from it measured 2.31:1, so --faint is deliberately the SAME value and the step below muted is made in type.

headline.purpose: Panel title and inspector head. Measured off the running shell's .main-view-title; hidden under .is-embedded because the rail and sidebar already name the surface.

title.purpose: The lede's answer and a fact's value — scannable without being a headline. 16px has no host equivalent and sits between body and heading.

body.purpose: Prose, rule names, section leads, verdicts. Capped at 74ch with text-wrap: balance.

small.purpose: Supporting facts, rails, prices, notes, JSON, a chain block's rows.

label.purpose: The third text step, made in TYPE and not in contrast: section names, fact labels, stage names, cause words, 'editando', badges, a chain block's own head, and the header's support note.

mono.purpose: Model ids, rails, counts, cooldown seconds, hashes, timestamps, context windows — anything an operator copies into a shell. A cause label is a phrase, so it is sans.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The host's own focus token, on :focus-visible everywhere. Not elevation.

shadows.name: state-halo
shadows.purpose: A 14%-alpha halo behind a 6px condition dot. Not elevation.

shadows.name: accent-rail
shadows.purpose: The one 'you picked this' mark: open row, matched rule, replayed step, picked decision.

shadows.name: dot-edge
shadows.purpose: Makes a raw-hue 6px dot locatable in a skin where the hue measures 1.38:1 against the plane.

borders.name: target-edge
borders.purpose: The only edge heavier than a hairline. Marks the row an instruction just sent the operator to (the chain row a 'swap for a catalogue model' warning named; the requirement field a warning named) inside a form of otherwise identical rows. A pointer, not a state — which is why it is not the 1px rail and not a plane.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing in the file.

motion.name: enter
motion.purpose: The only duration. One @keyframes (screen-in), used by the screen you asked for and reused by the in-row editor — a form arriving in a row and a screen arriving in the panel are the same event at two scales. Yields to prefers-reduced-motion.

extensions.colorMetaNote: Each entry also carries `value`: the FAIL-SAFE literal from inside its var() fallback — what the console looks like when the shell cannot be read at all. It is a documented value of this system, not drift, and it is recorded as a bare literal because a palette scan parses the whole var() expression and cannot see through it.

components.name: Out of Rotation Rows
components.description: Two kinds of absence in the same row primitive, told apart by what a control could honestly do. A MANUAL BAN is is-dead — raw-hue dot with its 1px inset edge, elo in mono, reason under it, the word 'banido' in the 45%-mixed bad form — and always carries 'Remover o bloqueio' in the action slot; the write is the whole manual_ban list minus the lifted item, because the server replaces lists wholesale. A BREAKER COOLDOWN is is-degraded with the time still owed in mono and NO control: it expires on its own, and a button promising to remove what time removes would be a false control. The confirmation lives after the group, so it survives the group hiding when the last ban goes.

Drawn in the UNORDERED chain form — no ordinals, no spine, wrapped across the line, keeping only the 26px indent — because the queue is a set and a numbered set lies about which elo runs first. It keeps the 11px tracked head every chain block uses, and renders nothing at all when it is empty or when nobody is out of rotation.

components.name: Finding With Its Remedy
components.description: An attempt whose model the catalogue never described: one note per unknown id, in the warn text step, naming the id and offering the two remedies that exist. 'Trocar por um modelo do catálogo' opens that group's chain editor with THAT attempt's row marked by the 3px accent target edge, so nobody counts rows; 'Deixar como está' writes nothing and hides the note until the next read. Both are ordinary full-face buttons — no accent on either, because neither is a commit.

components.name: Field, and the Inline Remedy
components.description: Mono, because these hold model ids, JSON and task text an operator pastes. Focus moves the border to the accent and the shared focus ring lands on the host's own token; 16px minimum under a coarse pointer, reached BY CLASS. The same primitive is the remedy on a broken row: a rule whose destination names a group that does not exist carries the ordinary destination select, labelled 'Escolha um destino que exista:', because the remedy for a broken value is the control that sets that value. It is present whenever the destination is missing and the rule is editable — no mode gates it.

components.description: Two destinations split by what the operator is DOING, drawn in the host's own nav idiom: a quiet muted label that takes the accent when selected, plus the host's 20px x 2px accent bar. Each tab carries the live state of what it leads to; a count appears only when counting something actionable, and wears amber when it counts exceptions.

components.name: Preset Choice
components.description: A real radio group, not characters drawn to look like one: each row is a label wrapping a real radio, so the whole row is the target and the browser's own arrow keys move between them. The chosen row takes the host's selected wash; the one in force says so on its own line in accent 11px.

components.name: Condition Line
components.description: A condition that needs an operator is a LINE marked with the same dot the tabs use — not a tinted card with a thick coloured edge. Every other group here is a hairline and space; the warning was the one element that disagreed, and it disagreed loudest. The muted-dot variant is a disclosure about the DATA, grey precisely so it can never read as an amber verdict, and it is the one place the missing count column's reason is stated.

verification.tests: 335 console tests, 62 extension tests, 4 nav tests; repository suite on Python 3.12 is 1770 passed / 2 skipped with a 100% coverage gate.

mechanicalDetector.afterThisFile: 7 advisory findings, all one thing, all accepted with reason — unchanged from the previous pass

accepted.why: Every one is a FAIL-SAFE, which is this surface's most load-bearing rule: there is no palette in the file, each token reads a --host-* property the theme bridge forwards, and the literal after the comma is what the console looks like when the shell cannot be read at all. The four hexes are the semantic four's fallbacks at the top of the stylesheet; the three rgb() values are the muted, line-strong and surface fallbacks, reported by the browser pass because that pass renders the console with no host around it — so every colour resolves to its fail-safe, which is precisely the degraded state the fallbacks exist for.
accepted.whyNotSilenced: The detector's colour reader only looks at `canonical` and `tonalRamp`, and it cannot see through a var() expression, so a fail-safe inside a fallback is unreachable to it. The two ways to clear the report would be to list the fail-safes as a tonal ramp — a lie about what they are — or to strip them from the stylesheet, which would leave an unstyled page whenever the theme bridge is missing. Neither is worth a clean scan. Each colorMeta entry also carries `value` with its bare fail-safe literal, which documents them explicitly even though this version of the colour check does not read that field.

verification.contrast: Everything this redesign added was measured in a browser with alpha compositing over the real host skins: worst case 4.9:1 in default/light, 10.13:1 in default/dark.
verification.mutation: 35 mutations applied to the new assertions; all 35 caught.
verification.notCanonized: Three things the build carries that are NOT system rules. (1) #editNote's copy: it says "o erro acima" while sitting in the header, which is ABOVE the banner it points at — a copy defect, recorded so it is fixed rather than imitated; the rule is that the note rides the same error set the banner reads. (2) The .55 opacity still on disabled buttons and scope pills, measured at 2.54:1 for a live Editar, which is exactly why the Nothing Live Is Dimmed rule exists — the value is a defect, not a token. (3) The WRITE map's surviving mode words (`done`, `stopEditing`) and the two historical 'compaction' comments: leftovers of features this build removed, kept out of the system because a phrase for a control that no longer exists is a landmine, not a vocabulary.

narrative.northStar: The Guest That Wears the House's Skin
narrative.overview:
This console is a panel inside Hermes One, and it owns no identity of its own. Every colour it paints reads a --host-* property the theme bridge forwards from the running shell, so it repaints with all 21 skins and both polarities; the hex after each comma is a fail-safe for a shell that cannot be read at all, not a palette. The measured reason: a copied palette is wrong in 20 skins out of 21, and in any light skin this console was a black rectangle inside a parchment shell — screenshotted.

It is an Operate surface: an operator's control room, not a dashboard. Groups are made of hairlines and space, never cards. The previous version of this file mandated a kicker + title + subtitle on every panel and a card around every block; that rule produced 53 cards, 21 subtitles and three competing health rollups, and the operator's verdict was "feio e muito poluído — pouco objetivo". Fewer elements, each carrying a fact.

The surface is TWO screens split by what the operator is DOING, not by which noun they are looking at. Configuração holds the policy — the ordered rule sheet, the probe, the model groups, the last-resort block, the presets, the general settings, the file editor — and every change is offered on the row it changes. Operação holds the runtime: reachable models, out-of-rotation, the decision log and its replay. Operação is not read-only by decree: it carries exactly one write, the Remover o bloqueio on a manual ban's own row, because that is state the operator put there and only that row can lift it. Three nouns (Tarefas / Modelos / Decisões) failed because no noun says where a setting lives. panel-health is gone; selectTab('health') survives as an alias to Operação, because a caller asking for the models is still asking for a screen that exists.
keyCharacteristics: No palette: every colour is the host's, forwarded live; the hexes are fail-safes.
The accent marks WHAT YOU PICKED; the semantic four report CONDITION. Never crossed.
Hairlines and space instead of cards; one structural primitive, the row.
Two type families — sans for prose and labels, mono for what an operator copies.
Writing is armed per object, on the row that owns it, in a fixed action slot; there is no mode, so a control is drawn whenever its object can carry it.
A finding that has a remedy carries the remedy on its own row.
No <svg> in the document and no markup injection: a control is a word.
Two screens, one column, 100dvh, 44px targets and 16px inputs under a coarse pointer.

rules.name: The No Palette Rule
rules.body: No colour is authored here. If a value cannot be traced to a --host-* property, it is not a token — it is a bug, and the only hexes in the file are the fail-safes for an unreadable shell.

rules.name: The Split Meaning Rule
rules.body: The accent reports SELECTION; the four report CONDITION. A gold underline can therefore never be read as health, and a green dot can never be read as selection. A fifth meaning (predicate family, billing mode, destination kind) gets no hue at all — it is made in TYPE and PLANE, plus its own word.

rules.name: The 45% Mix Rule
rules.body: A state colour has two forms and the difference is measured. The host's success/warning/error/info are authored for FILLS; as text on their own skin's background they bottom out at 1.38:1 (info, neon-paint/light). So a DOT takes the raw hue plus a 1px inset edge on the strong hairline, and a WORD takes the -text form: 45% hue into the skin's TEXT. 45% clears 4.5:1 in every skin (worst 5.08:1) where 50% does not (4.44:1); mixing toward text rather than away from background is what makes it darken on parchment and lighten on navy.

rules.name: The Two Text Steps Rule
rules.body: --faint is deliberately the same value as --muted, because --host-muted already bottoms out at 3.47:1 and a third step derived from it measured 2.31:1. The step below muted is made in TYPE — 11px uppercase tracked, the host's own metadata treatment — never in contrast.

rules.name: The Colour Budget Rule
rules.body: Only a refusal is painted. Rejection reasons under a DROPPED heading stay muted (the heading already says they were refused; painting them put three reds beside the one real refusal); "goes to the classifier" is a KIND of destination and is named once on its stage heading rather than coloured five times. An off-catalogue attempt is a finding in a warn-text note, not a red row: the model still runs.

rules.name: The Never The Only Channel Rule
rules.body: Every dot sits beside its state in words; every multiplier is in the text beside its amber. Colour is confirmation, never the fact.

rules.name: The Amber Is A Verdict Rule
rules.body: Amber means the ROUTER needs attention — an exception count, a rule that never fired, an expensive window, a missing billing mode, an id the catalogue does not know. It never marks the operator's own doing (an open editor is not a degradation), and a disclosure about the DATA rather than the policy takes the muted dot instead.

rules.name: The Copy-It Rule
rules.body: Sans carries prose, labels and section names; mono carries machine facts. A cause label ("fail safe strong") is a phrase, so it is sans. A rule title is prose and its slug is a machine fact, so they do not share one face — at one size in one mono they made the pt-BR name and the id peers and left the row with no step of its own.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on the body, so counts line up down a column.

rules.name: The One Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose is capped at 74ch with text-wrap: balance, and the cap is attached to the KIND of content, not to a particular class: a measure that belongs to a class only holds where that class went, and prose kept landing elsewhere. At full panel width lines ran to 146 characters, twice a readable line. balance and not pretty: measured on this surface, pretty left last lines at 24%, 13% and 5% of the first line's width; balance puts them at 91–95%. Data is exempt on purpose — chain rows, chips, the Ordem: knob line and every mono value, which a measure would only wrap.

rules.name: The Label Is Not A Sentence Rule
rules.body: Tracked uppercase is a treatment for a label; 58 characters of it is a passage read by shape, so a sentence goes to a placeholder or a note instead.

rules.name: The Sequence Down One Spine Rule
rules.body: The policy is an ordered first-match table and a trace is a short ordered path, so both are drawn as numbered vertical lines against a single 1px spine — never as a node canvas. Fifteen tiny boxes to highlight three of them makes the reader hunt for the answer.

rules.name: The Unordered Gets No Ordinals Rule
rules.body: A sequential chain is numbered down the spine; a random chain is a SET — it loses the ordinals and the spine and wraps across the line, keeping only the 26px indent so the eye does not have to re-find the model. A numbered random chain is a lie about which elo runs first. The substitute queue on Operação is drawn in that same unordered form.

rules.name: The Compare Down A Column Rule
rules.body: Destination and count are fixed tracks. Two ways this has failed, both measured: auto on the destination track sized to its content's intrinsic width (278px) and starved the minmax(0, 1fr) rule column to 0px; and capping the CHILD with a percentage is circular — the child's containing block is a track the child itself sizes, so the destination resolved to 0px and every destination word vanished while the arrow stayed. The cap belongs on the TRACK.

rules.name: The No Card Without A Reason Rule
rules.body: A card exists to group things read together. One list, one table or one control does not need a frame, and nothing gets a second frame inside something already marked — the in-row editor is a raised plane with one hairline, not a box inside a box.

rules.name: The 1px Accent Rail Rule
rules.body: Every "you picked this" mark is the same object: an inset 1px accent rail on the leading edge, plus the accent wash where a whole row is chosen. The open row, the probed rule that matched, the replayed trace step, the picked decision — one reading, learned once. Its one louder sibling is the 3px accent left edge on a row an instruction just sent the operator to, which is a pointer and not a state.

rules.name: The Nothing Live Is Dimmed Rule
rules.body: No element is faded by opacity while its own controls stay pressable. Measured at .55 on parchment: Editar fell to 2.54:1 and the row title to 3.95:1, against a 4.5:1 floor. Dimming survives only where nothing in the dimmed thing can be pressed — a rule switched off in the file, a trace step still ahead of the reader.

rules.name: The Render Nothing For Nothing Rule
rules.body: No empty card, no dashed placeholder, no row that announces its own emptiness. A section with no data is absent (the out-of-rotation group, the substitute queue inside it, the clock strip, the count column, the whole last-resort block) or a single muted line. A count column with nothing to count is not built at all — not filled with em dashes, and not left with a branch that renders a placeholder no reader ever sees.

rules.name: The One Write Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: One WRITE map owns every phrase the screen says — not just the write verbs (plan, save, saving, revert, cancel, conflict, no-op, in-flight, lint error, missing action, no credential) but loading, refresh/refreshing, routing/routingOn/routingOff, banned, cooldownLeft, classifier, textEdit, and the named gesture remove/removing. Static markup carries none of it: one pass at boot stamps the file editor's three buttons, the reload button and the file editor's own note from the map, and the draft hint quotes the buttons by the map's labels. The defect it prevents is a phrase existing twice in the file — a test counts each literal — and the reason a gesture is named twice (resting and in flight) is so a refusal reads "não é possível remover o bloqueio", never a generic "salvar" that does not match the button that was pressed.

rules.name: The Control Only For What A Control Can Do Rule
rules.body: A row gets a button only where pressing it changes the thing named. A manual ban gets Remover o bloqueio; a breaker cooldown gets nothing, because it lapses on its own. Offering to remove what time removes is a lie the surface tells once and the operator remembers.

rules.name: The Remedy On The Row Rule
rules.body: A finding that has a remedy carries the remedy where the finding is. A destination naming a group that does not exist carries the destination select. An attempt the catalogue does not know names the id and offers the two things that exist: swap it for a catalogue model — which opens that group's chain editor with THAT attempt's row marked, so nobody counts rows — or leave it, which writes nothing and hides the note until the next read. Two remedies, both real; a warning with no way out is a dead end, and this console was rebuilt to remove them.

rules.name: The One Attach Point Rule
rules.body: The editor is a singleton. Where one object is shown in two places, the second place links to the first and never opens a second form: two attach points for one form mean it lands in whichever renderer ran last.

rules.name: The Ranked, Not Recited Rule
rules.body: Where a thing has five knobs and four are the engine's default, the DECLARED ones are the line and the defaults collapse into one control that says how many there are. Recited inline they read 170 characters in which the same parenthesis appears three times and one knob is news.

rules.name: The Count, Not A Sentence Rule
rules.body: A count column holds a count ("26×", "nunca") and its cell is NOT BUILT when the log does not cover the policy — the track collapses and the reason is stated once, by the disclosure above the list. Never per row: the sentence form put the same 60 characters on ten consecutive rows in the widest column and overflowed the host panel by 236px with the third column clipped. Because the cell is absent in that case, a "stale" branch inside the cell is unreachable by construction and does not exist.

rules.name: The Editor Node Is Fetched, Never Held Rule
rules.body: The form is a singleton moved next to whatever is being edited, so it becomes a child of a row that the next render clears. It is fetched through an accessor that rebuilds it under the same id when the document no longer has one. Measured in a browser: without it, the first Editar built a form and every one after it marked a row and rendered nothing.

rules.name: The Browser's Own Surfaces Take The Skin Rule
rules.body: Selection, caret and scrollbars are drawn too: a default blue selection inside a gold-on-navy shell, a white caret and a platform-grey scrollbar belong to no design system.

dos: Do read every colour from a --host-* property, and treat the hex after the comma as the fail-safe for an unreadable shell.
Do keep the accent for selection and the four for condition, and give a fifth distinction TYPE and PLANE plus its own word instead of a hue.
Do write a state as a word in the 45%-mixed -text form, and a state as a dot in the raw hue with a 1px inset edge — with the word always beside the dot.
Do make groups out of a heading, one hairline and space, at 34px apart, with more space above a heading than below it.
Do put every editable object's own control in the fixed 84px action slot, and open its form inside the row it changes.
Do draw a control whenever its object exists — nothing on this surface is gated on a mode, because there is no mode left to arm.
Do give a finding its remedy on its own row, and mark the row an instruction sent the operator to with the 3px accent edge.
Do keep every phrase the screen says in the WRITE map, and stamp static labels from it at boot.
Do cap prose at 74ch with text-wrap: balance, attached to the kind of content rather than to a class, and leave data uncapped.
Do draw an ordered sequence numbered down one 1px spine, and an unordered one as a wrapped set with no ordinals.
Do keep the domain's words — profile, model, provider/rail, tier, rule, classifier, fail-safe, blocklist, breaker, decision — and invent none.
Do keep 100dvh, 44px coarse-pointer targets, and max(16px, 1em) inputs named BY CLASS.
donts: Don't author a palette, a wordmark, or a type step the host does not ship. The 10.5px and 20px steps were a guest's scale and read as an accident beside host chrome.
Don't frame a single list, table or control, and don't put a frame inside something already marked as open or picked.
Don't derive a third, fainter text step: measured at 2.31:1. Make the step in type instead.
Don't fade anything by opacity while its own controls stay pressable — measured 2.54:1 for a live Editar at .55.
Don't paint every reason, every destination kind, or the operator's own actions. Amber is a verdict about the router; a disclosure about the DATA takes the muted dot.
Don't add a global mode, or any control whose scope is not the thing you can see. Arming the old one changed the page by 0 characters.
Don't offer a control for something that resolves itself — a breaker cooldown gets a countdown, never a button.
Don't open a second editor for an object that already has one; link to it.
Don't disable a control that must not be pressed if it can be absent instead, and don't build a cell only to fill it with em dashes or a branch nobody reaches.
Don't put a write's confirmation inside a block that hides when the write succeeds.
Don't let a phrase exist twice in the file, or let static markup own a word the WRITE map should.

Don't use <svg> or an icon font in this document, and never innerHTML / insertAdjacentHTML / outerHTML / document.write — decision traces carry attacker-influenceable task text, so all text goes through textContent. A control is a word. (The rail icon the extension registers with the host is the host's own iconPath API, outside this document.)
Don't size a destination or count column with auto, or cap it on the child: both collapsed the column to 0px, measured.

Don't repeat a fact two surfaces already own — a second chip for a state something else signals, a badge counting what a numbered list counts, a heading repeating the panel title, or a per-row copy of the window a count was taken over.

Don't add a second @keyframes, a second button vocabulary, or a second chip shape. One authored moment (160ms ease-out on the screen you asked for, reused by the in-row form), and it yields to prefers-reduced-motion.
